1.title: Standards and Frameworks: OECD, NIST and ISO
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Standards and Frameworks. This is competency D of domain two. After the laws, you now meet the tools that organizations use to organize their work. They are the O E C D principles, the N I S T A I Risk Management Framework and its Playbook, and the three core I S O standards.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Explain the O E C D principles, the policy recommendations and the recommended practices. Explain the N I S T A I R M F: its functions, categories and subcategories, and the Playbook. Explain the three core I S O standards: twenty-two nine eight nine, forty-two thousand and one, and forty-two thousand and five. And tell law, standard and framework apart, and say how they fit together.

1.title: Case Check-In: One Stack for Helios
1.text: At Helios, Samira Haddad's committee must choose how to organize the program. It picks I S O forty-two thousand and one to structure the program, the N I S T A I R M F to run risk on each system, and the E U A I Act as the legal floor. It bases its policy on the O E C D principles. You must explain what each instrument is for, and why they do not compete.

1.title: The OECD AI Principles: Origin and Role
1.text: This slide is tagged dates. The O E C D is an intergovernmental organization. Its Recommendation on A I is a non-binding standard that many governments follow. It was first adopted in twenty nineteen and updated in May, twenty twenty-four. It sets five values-based principles for A I actors, and five recommendations for policy-makers. Its definition of an A I system, which we met in module one, was reused in other laws and frameworks. It is soft law. Exam tip: the principles are values, not a certification or a statute.

1.title: The Five Values-Based Principles
1.text: The O E C D has five values-based principles. One point one: inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being, with responsible stewardship of trustworthy A I. One point two: human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy, with safeguards such as human oversight. One point three: transparency and explainability, with responsible disclosure. One point four: robustness, security and safety across the whole lifecycle, with the ability to override, repair or decommission safely. One point five: accountability, with traceability and a systematic risk management approach to each phase. Exam tip: safe decommissioning is a practical hook.

1.title: Recommendations for Policy-Makers
1.text: The O E C D also makes five recommendations to governments. Two point one: invest in A I research and development. Two point two: foster an inclusive A I-enabling ecosystem. Two point three: shape an enabling, interoperable governance and policy environment. Two point four: build human capacity and prepare for labor-market transformation. Two point five: international co-operation for trustworthy A I. Organizations meet these through policy engagement and skills programs. Exam tip: principles are for A I actors. Recommendations are for governments.

1.title: The OECD Framework and Recommended Practices
1.text: The O E C D also offers a framework and practices. Its classification framework describes an A I system along five dimensions: people and planet, economic context, data and input, A I model, and task and output. N I S T adapted it for its own lifecycle figure. For organizations, recommended practices include risk management in each lifecycle phase, traceability of data, processes and decisions, and responsible business conduct with suppliers. Systems that cause undue harm can be overridden, repaired or decommissioned. Exam tip: the framework describes a system. It is not a checklist.

1.title: The NIST AI RMF at a Glance
1.text: This slide is tagged dates and verify live. N I S T released A I R M F one point zero in January, twenty twenty-three. It is voluntary, sector-agnostic, and meant to be a living document, with a formal review expected no later than twenty twenty-eight. Part one gives foundations: framing A I risk, the audience, trustworthy characteristics and effectiveness. Part two is the Core: four functions, nineteen categories and seventy-two subcategories, followed by profiles. The online Playbook suggests actions, and the generative A I profile applies it to generative A I. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, N I S T says the framework is being updated.

1.title: The Seven Trustworthy Characteristics
1.text: The N I S T framework names seven characteristics of trustworthy A I. Valid and reliable is the foundation. Then safe, and secure and resilient. Accountable and transparent runs through all of them. Then explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed. Tradeoffs among them are usual, so balance them by context and justify the choice openly. Trustworthiness is only as strong as its weakest characteristic. Exam tip: if the system is not valid and reliable, nothing above it helps.

1.title: The Core: Four Functions
1.text: The Core has four functions. GOVERN is cross-cutting: culture, policies, accountability and structures. MAP frames the context and risks of a specific system. MEASURE analyzes, assesses and tracks risks with metrics and tests. MANAGE prioritizes and treats risks, with response and recovery. The actions are not a checklist and need no fixed order. After GOVERN is in place, most users start with MAP, then MEASURE and MANAGE, and iterate. Exam tip: GOVERN applies to everything. The other three apply system by system.

1.title: GOVERN: Culture, Accountability and Policy
1.text: GOVERN has six categories and nineteen subcategories. Govern one covers policies, processes and practices, including legal requirements, risk tolerance, inventory and decommissioning. Govern two covers accountability structures, roles, training and executive responsibility. Govern three covers diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility. Govern four covers a culture that considers and communicates A I risk. Govern five covers engagement with relevant A I actors. Govern six covers third-party software, data and supply chain. Modules two and three used several, such as Govern two point one and Govern six point one. Exam tip: GOVERN is not tied to one system.

1.title: MAP: Context and Impacts
1.text: MAP has five categories and eighteen subcategories. Map one: context is established and understood, including intended purposes, laws and settings. Map two: the A I system is categorized by its tasks and methods. Map three: capabilities, usage, goals, benefits and costs are understood against benchmarks. Map four: risks and benefits of all components, including third-party. Map five: impacts on individuals, groups, communities, organizations and society. MAP ends with enough context to inform an initial go or no-go decision. Exam tip: who is affected and what is it for? That is MAP.

2.title: MEASURE: Metrics, Testing and Tracking
2.text: MEASURE has four categories and twenty-two subcategories. Measure one: appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied. Measure two: the system is evaluated for trustworthy characteristics. Measure three: mechanisms track identified risks over time. Measure four: feedback about the efficacy of measurement is gathered. It uses quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods, and systems are tested before deployment and regularly in operation. Measure two point eleven covers fairness and bias. Independent review improves testing. Exam tip: measuring shows whether a risk is real. MANAGE decides what to do.

2.title: MANAGE: Prioritize, Respond and Recover
2.text: MANAGE has four categories and thirteen subcategories. Manage one: risks are prioritized, responded to and managed. Manage two: strategies to maximize benefits and minimize impacts. Manage three: third-party risks and benefits. Manage four: risk treatments, response, recovery and communication plans. Manage one point two prioritizes treatment by impact, likelihood and resources. Manage two point four sets mechanisms to supersede, disengage or deactivate systems. Manage four point one covers post-deployment monitoring plans, with appeal and override, decommissioning and incident response. Exam tip: deactivation and incident response are MANAGE.

2.title: The Playbook, Profiles and the Generative AI Profile
2.text: This is a beyond-the-Body-of-Knowledge slide, tagged dates and verify live. The Playbook offers suggested actions for each subcategory. It is voluntary, not a checklist, and a living resource updated about twice a year. Profiles tailor the Core. A use-case profile applies it to a setting, such as hiring. Temporal profiles describe a current and a target state, and the gap becomes the action plan. Cross-sectoral profiles cover topics such as large language models. The generative A I profile, from July twenty twenty-four, defines twelve generative A I risks. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, the Playbook will follow the framework's update.

2.title: ISO/IEC 22989: A Shared Language
2.text: I S O twenty-two nine eight nine sets out A I concepts and terminology: what terms such as A I system, machine learning, bias and robustness mean. It describes stakeholder roles across the A I value chain and lifecycle concepts. Its A I system definition, an engineered system generating outputs for human-defined objectives, feeds N I S T and other documents. It is a vocabulary standard: no requirements, and no certification. This course teaches it from the Body of Knowledge and public summaries, because the standard is paid. Exam tip: twenty-two nine eight nine is the dictionary.

2.title: ISO/IEC 42001: The AI Management System
2.text: This slide is tagged dates. I S O forty-two thousand and one, published in December twenty twenty-three, sets requirements for an A I management system: an organization-wide system to govern A I responsibly. It follows the same harmonized structure as I S O twenty-seven thousand and one and nine thousand and one: clauses four to ten, in a plan-do-check-act cycle. Four is context, five leadership and A I policy, six planning, including risk and impact assessment, seven support, eight operation, nine performance evaluation, and ten improvement. It is certifiable by accredited bodies. The depth here comes from public summaries. Exam tip: a management system is a continuing process.

2.title: ISO/IEC 42001: Controls and Certification
2.text: Annex A is a reference set of thirty-eight controls in nine control objectives, covering topics such as A I policy, internal organization, resources, impact assessment, life cycle, data, information for parties, use, and third-party relationships. Selection is risk-based: the organization chooses controls and records its choices in a statement of applicability. Annex B gives implementation guidance, Annex C lists A I-related risk sources, and Annex D covers sectors. An accredited body audits the system and certifies it. The certificate shows the management system meets the standard, not that a product is safe or legal. Exam tip: it is not proof of legal compliance.

2.title: ISO/IEC 42005: AI System Impact Assessment
2.text: This slide is tagged dates. I S O forty-two thousand and five, published on the twenty-seventh of May, twenty twenty-five, gives guidance, not requirements, for A I system impact assessment. It covers how and when to assess how a system and its foreseeable uses may affect individuals and society, at which life-cycle stages, and how to document, approve and review the result. It suits organizations of any size, and the assessment can be integrated with A I risk management and the management system. Forty-two thousand and one asks for impact assessment. Forty-two thousand and five explains how to do it. Exam tip: one requires, the other guides.

2.title: Law, Standard, Framework: How They Fit
2.text: How do they fit together? The E U A I Act is binding law, with duties and penalties, and Helios's legal floor. The O E C D principles are soft law, shaping policy, and Helios's policy basis. The N I S T A I R M F is a voluntary framework, a risk process run system by system. I S O forty-two thousand and one is a certifiable standard, the management structure of the program. Twenty-two nine eight nine is vocabulary, and forty-two thousand and five is impact-assessment guidance. I S O twenty-three thousand eight hundred ninety-four gives guidance on A I risk management. Only law is mandatory. Exam tip: know what kind of instrument it is.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Let us recap. The O E C D has five principles: inclusive growth; human rights, fairness and privacy; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; and accountability. It also has five policy recommendations. The N I S T A I R M F is voluntary, with four functions, nineteen categories and seventy-two subcategories. GOVERN cuts across, and MAP leads to MEASURE and MANAGE. The Playbook and profiles tailor it. I S O has a vocabulary, a certifiable management system, and impact-assessment guidance. And only law is binding.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Which list correctly names the O E C D's five values-based principles for trustworthy A I? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. They are inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being; human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; and accountability. The other lists swap in items that are not O E C D principles.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Helios's committee wants to document the intended purpose, the legal context, the affected groups and the expected benefits of the new assistant before it is tested. Which N I S T A I R M F function does this belong to? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. MAP establishes context: purposes, legal context, settings, benefits and impacts on people. MEASURE comes after, and MANAGE treats the risks.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Which two statements about the N I S T A I R M F Playbook are correct? Select two. The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and E. The Playbook offers voluntary suggested actions aligned to the Core's subcategories, and organizations tailor them. It is not mandatory, not a certification scheme, and not a replacement for the Core.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. How does I S O forty-two thousand and one differ from the N I S T A I R M F? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. I S O forty-two thousand and one specifies requirements for an A I management system, and it is certifiable by accredited bodies. The N I S T framework is voluntary guidance with no certification. Neither is a binding law.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all four answers. Question one: D. Question two: C. Question three: B and E. Question four: D. That completes Module seven, and with it domain two. Next, domain three begins with Module eight: governing the design and build of an A I system.
